21	## 0. Decisions at a glance
22	
23	| # | Decision | Section |
24	|---|----------|---------|
25	| D1 | Definitional Pic = Čech H¹ of the units presheaf on the small Zariski site: **pointed covers** (one open per point), built **on mathlib's `PresheafOfGroups.H1`** fixed-family layer, refinement colimit as a sigma-type quotient, everything in `Type u`. | §2 |
26	| D2 | Group structure **multiplicative**, `CommGroup` carriers, `CommGrpCat.{u}`-valued functors. | §2.4 |
27	| D3 | Relative functor = H_T-coset quotient `Pic((C ⊗ T).left) ⧸ range(snd-pullback)` on `(Over (Spec k))ᵒᵖ`, `CommGrpCat.{u}`-valued. Never the absolute `Pic(C×T)`. | §3 |

36	## 1. Standing conventions
37	
38	- **Universe discipline: everything at `u`.** `Scheme.{u}`, test category `Over (Spec (.of k))`
39	  with hom-types in `Type u`, all Pic carriers in `Type u`, all functors valued in
40	  `CommGrpCat.{u}`. This is forced by `GrpObj.ofRepresentableBy`
41	  (`Mathlib/CategoryTheory/Monoidal/Cartesian/Grp.lean:35`), which couples the universe of the
42	  representing object's homs with the functor's value universe (survey "Universe landmines").
43	  `JacobianData C` itself lives in `Type (u+1)` (it contains a scheme); that is harmless.
44	- **Hypothesis bundle.** Every file uses the frozen variable block
45	  `{k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k))) [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom]
46	  [IsProper C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]`, plus the Wave-1 derived instance
47	  `GeometricallyIntegral C.hom` (route Wave-1 item 2) whenever integrality is used.
48	- **Product language.** All products of test objects are the cartesian-monoidal product in
49	  `Over (Spec (.of k))` (`CategoryTheory/Monoidal/Cartesian/Over.lean:34`,
50	  `Over.cartesianMonoidalCategory`, chosen via `Limits.pullback`): `C ⊗ T`, projections
51	  `fst C T`, `snd C T`, whiskering `C ◁ g`. This is the vocabulary of the frozen file
52	  (`𝟙_ (Over (Spec (.of k)))`, `η[·]`, `Functor.LaxMonoidal.ε`). Descents to `Scheme`-level
53	  pullbacks (`(C ⊗ T).left`) happen only inside cocycle constructions, with the bridge lemmas
54	  confined to `Picard/RelFunctor.lean`. Known wall: `Over.pullback` instance opacity — use the
55	  route rule 9 fixes (point-level `congrArg` calc chains, `erw [Category.comp_id]`).
56	- **Verification bar** (route rule 7): `lake build <Module>` kernel check, then `lean_verify`
57	  axiom audit (`propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound` only) on each keystone. LSP advisory only.
58	- Category names verified in the v4.31 checkout: bundled concrete categories are `GrpCat`,
59	  `CommGrpCat`, `CommMonCat` (e.g. `CommMonCat.units : CommMonCat.{u} ⥤ CommGrpCat.{u}`,
60	  `Mathlib/Algebra/Category/Grp/Adjunctions.lean:202`); bundled group *objects* are
61	  `CategoryTheory.Grp C` (`Mathlib/CategoryTheory/Monoidal/Grp.lean:82`), the challenge's
62	  `Grp (Over (Spec (.of k)))`.

65	
66	## 2. (A) The definitional Pic carrier
67	
68	**Semantic pin.** For any scheme `X`, the Picard group *of record* is the Čech cohomology
69	`Ȟ¹(X, 𝒪_X^*)` on the small Zariski site: covers by opens, unit-valued 1-cocycles modulo
70	coboundaries, colimit over refinement. This is recon lesson 1 verbatim, and it is Kleiman's own
71	remark `rk:coh` (§2.11): "for any ringed space `R`, there is a natural isomorphism
72	`Pic(R) = H¹(R, 𝒪_R^*)`" (his eq. 2.11.2 = `eq:2b`, citing Hartshorne III Ex. 4.5).
73	
74	**Semantic-honesty remark (record in the blueprint chapter).** The frozen `Challenge.lean` never
75	mentions `Pic`, line bundles, or invertible sheaves; the only consumers of the carrier are the
76	functors and elements defined in this spec. Therefore the comparison
77	"`CechPic X ≃ {invertible 𝒪_X-modules}/≅`" is **Phase-2 optional** (a `ForMathlib` PR
78	candidate), and no Wave depends on it. What is **Phase-1 mandatory** is that `𝒪(D)`-classes of
79	relative effective divisors be constructible as explicit cocycles from local equations, because
80	`ofCurve` is pinned as `t ↦ [𝒪(Γ_t − P_T)]` (route §3). §2.6 pins that constructor.
81	
82	### 2.1 Index discipline: pointed covers, arbitrary opens
83	
84	```lean
85	/-- A pointed open cover of a scheme: one open per point, containing it. -/
86	structure Scheme.PointedCover (X : Scheme.{u}) : Type u where
87	  opens : X → X.Opens
88	  mem_opens : ∀ x, x ∈ opens x
89	```
90	
91	with the refinement preorder `𝒱 ≤ 𝒰 ↔ ∀ x, 𝒱.opens x ≤ 𝒰.opens x`.
92	
93	Decision rationale (each alternative was weighed):
94	
95	- **Not finite covers, not affine covers, not `Set X.Opens`.** Pointed covers give:
96	  (a) *smallness for free* — the index type is the fixed carrier `X : Type u`, so the sigma type
97	  in §2.3 stays in `Type u`; (b) *canonical refinement maps* — a refinement `𝒱 ≤ 𝒰` refines
98	  **indexwise** (`𝒱.opens x ≤ 𝒰.opens x`), so the cocycle-restriction map needs no choice of a
99	  reindexing function and no "independence of the refinement map" lemma at the carrier level;
100	  (c) *directedness by pointwise `⊓`* (`(𝒰 ⊓ 𝒱).opens x := 𝒰.opens x ⊓ 𝒱.opens x`), so the
101	  refinement colimit is filtered; (d) *clean pullback* — for `f : X ⟶ Y` the pulled-back cover is
102	  `x ↦ f ⁻¹ᵁ (𝒰.opens (f x))`, again pointed, again indexed by the carrier. Affineness
103	  constraints would break (d) (preimages of affines are not affine); `Set`-indexing breaks (b)
104	  (pullback collapses indices).
105	- Affine or finite covers re-enter as *cofinality lemmas*, not as carrier structure: every
106	  pointed cover is refined by a pointed affine cover (`x ↦` an affine open neighbourhood inside
107	  `𝒰.opens x`; the choice lives inside a `Prop`, so no data escapes). This is where the
108	  2-cover computations of the χ-ledger and the T₀ engine plug in.
109	
110	### 2.2 The cocycle layer: build on `PresheafOfGroups.H1`
111	
112	**Decision: build on mathlib's fixed-family layer**, not hand-rolled. Instantiation:
113	
114	```lean
115	/-- The units presheaf of a scheme, on its small Zariski site. -/
116	def Scheme.unitsPresheaf (X : Scheme.{u}) : (X.Opens)ᵒᵖ ⥤ CommGrpCat.{u} :=
117	  X.presheaf ⋙ forget₂ CommRingCat CommMonCat ⋙ CommMonCat.units
118	-- (OPEN-4: if the `forget₂ CommRingCat CommMonCat` path is absent in v4.31, a ~20-line
119	-- bespoke functor replaces the composition; the statement shape is unchanged.)
120	
121	abbrev Scheme.unitsCocycle (X : Scheme.{u}) (𝒰 : X.PointedCover) :=
122	  PresheafOfGroups.OneCocycle (X.unitsPresheaf ⋙ forget₂ CommGrpCat GrpCat) 𝒰.opens
123	```
124	
125	Here the site category is the poset `X.Opens`, the family is `𝒰.opens : X → X.Opens`, and
126	mathlib's `OneCochain/OneCocycle/OneCohomologyRelation/IsCohomologous/H1` + `One (H1 G U)`
127	(`Mathlib/CategoryTheory/Sites/NonabelianCohomology/H1.lean:58–197`) come for free. On a poset
128	with infima, the `ev (i j) (a : T ⟶ U i) (b : T ⟶ U j)`-style cochain is *equivalent* to the
129	classical pair data `g x y ∈ 𝒪ˣ(𝒰x ⊓ 𝒰y)` with the cocycle condition on triple infima: homs
130	are subsingletons, so `ev` is determined by its value at `T = 𝒰x ⊓ 𝒰y` via `ev_precomp`, and
131	`ev_trans` at the triple infimum is the classical condition. **Binding ergonomic requirement**:
132	`Picard/CechH1.lean` must provide the two-way bridge so lane agents never touch `ev` directly:
133	
134	```lean
135	/-- Build a 1-cocycle over a poset with binary infima from classical pair data. -/
136	def PresheafOfGroups.OneCocycle.ofPairs
137	    (g : ∀ x y, G.obj (op (𝒰.opens x ⊓ 𝒰.opens y)))
138	    (hg : ∀ x y z, /- restrictions to the triple infimum satisfy g x y · g y z = g x z -/) :
139	    OneCocycle G 𝒰.opens
140	lemma ev_inf (γ : OneCocycle G 𝒰.opens) (x y) : γ.ev x y ⋯ = ⋯   -- extraction at the infimum
141	```
142	
143	Additions ours to make (all in `Picard/CechH1.lean`, stated generically over any `Cᵒᵖ ⥤
144	CommGrpCat.{w}` — a mathlib-PR candidate, their file's TODO list asks for exactly this):
145	
146	- `Mul/Inv/CommGroup (OneCocycle Gc U)` when the presheaf is commutative-group-valued (the
147	  product of cocycles satisfies `ev_trans` only using commutativity), and the descended
148	  `CommGroup (H1 Gc U)` via `Quot.map₂` (compatibility of `IsCohomologous` with products again
149	  uses commutativity).
150	- Restriction along an indexwise refinement `res : H1 G 𝒰 →* H1 G 𝒱` for `𝒱 ≤ 𝒰`
151	  (on cocycles: restrict values along the inclusions; strictly functorial:
152	  `res_res : res h₂ ∘ res h₁ = res (h₁.trans h₂)` holds on the nose at cochain level).
153	
154	### 2.3 The refinement colimit
155	
156	```lean
157	/-- The definitional Picard group: Čech H¹ of the units presheaf, colimit over pointed covers. -/
158	def Scheme.CechPic (X : Scheme.{u}) : Type u :=
159	  Quot (fun p q : (Σ 𝒰 : X.PointedCover, PresheafOfGroups.H1 ⋯ 𝒰.opens) =>
160	    ∃ 𝒲, ∃ (h₁ : 𝒲 ≤ p.1) (h₂ : 𝒲 ≤ q.1), res h₁ p.2 = res h₂ q.2)
161	```
162	
163	- The relation is an equivalence *because the poset is directed* (common refinement by pointwise
164	  `⊓`) and `res` strictly composes; the standard filtered-colimit argument is elementary and
165	  choice-free.
166	- Universe accounting: `X.PointedCover : Type u`, each `H1 … : Type u` (index `X : Type u`,
167	  values in `Type u`), the sigma is `Type u`, the quotient is `Type u`. **No `ULift` anywhere.**
168	- `CommGroup (X.CechPic)`: multiplication of classes represented on a common refinement;
169	  well-definedness from §2.2's `CommGroup (H1 …)` + `res` being a group hom.
170	- Constructor/eliminator API: `CechPic.mk (𝒰) (γ : OneCocycle …) : X.CechPic`,
171	  `CechPic.ind`, `CechPic.mk_eq_mk_iff_of_refines`, and the "sanity gate"
172	  `CechPic (Spec (.of K)) ≃* PUnit`-style triviality for fields (one-point space, one cover,
173	  `ev_refl` kills every cocycle) — this is Lane 1's cheap end-to-end test.
174	
175	### 2.4 Group structure: multiplicative, `CommGrpCat`-valued
176	
177	**Decision: multiplicative.** Justification (each item load-bearing):
178	
179	1. The cocycle values are *units of rings*; their native structure is multiplicative, and
180	   `tensor product of line bundles = pointwise multiplication of transition units`,
181	   `dual = pointwise inverse` — recon lesson 1's entire point. An additive carrier would
182	   re-introduce a translation layer at exactly the spot the old draft burned.
183	2. `GrpObj.ofRepresentableBy` takes `F : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ GrpCat.{w}` — multiplicative — and
184	   `forget₂ CommGrpCat GrpCat` is the canonical bridge. The old draft's
185	   `AddCommGrpCat.{u+1}` choice cost both a universe bump and an additive/multiplicative
186	   mismatch at the representability gate.
187	3. Mathlib's `PresheafOfGroups.H1` layer (§2.2) is multiplicative.
188	
189	The `ℤ`-valued *degree* (§6) is additive; the interface between the multiplicative Pic and the
190	additive degree is a single `→ ℤ` map with `deg (a * b) = deg a + deg b` — pinned as such, no
191	`Multiplicative ℤ` gymnastics in consumer-facing statements.
192	
193	### 2.5 Functoriality: pullback of cocycles
194	
195	```lean
196	def Scheme.CechPic.map {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) : Y.CechPic →* X.CechPic
197	theorem Scheme.CechPic.map_id (X) : CechPic.map (𝟙 X) = MonoidHom.id _
198	theorem Scheme.CechPic.map_comp (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y ⟶ Z) :
199	    CechPic.map (f ≫ g) = (CechPic.map f).comp (CechPic.map g)
200	```
201	
202	On representatives: pull the cover back pointwise through `f.base` (`x ↦ f ⁻¹ᵁ 𝒰.opens (f x)`),
203	pull the units back through `f.app`, restrict. `map_comp` compares the covers
204	`(f ≫ g) ⁻¹ᵁ 𝒰 (g (f x))` and `f ⁻¹ᵁ (g ⁻¹ᵁ 𝒰 (g (f x)))` — equal opens
205	(`Scheme.preimage_comp`), with the value comparison through `Scheme.Hom.app_comp`; if defeq
206	friction appears, prove it through the refinement relation (both sides restrict to a common
207	refinement) rather than `eqToHom` surgery.
208	
209	### 2.6 Divisor classes as cocycles: the `𝒪(D)` constructor
210	
211	Three constructors, in dependency order. Sign convention (route §3, audited in §8):
212	a local-equation system `(fᵢ)` for an effective `D` produces the class of `𝒪(D)` with
213	transition units `g x y = f x / f y` on overlaps (trivialization of `𝒪(D)` on `𝒰x` by
214	multiplication by `f x`).
215	
216	**(a) Local-equation data → class** (`Picard/DivisorClass.lean`):
217	
218	```lean
219	/-- Local equations for an effective Cartier divisor, adapted to a pointed cover. -/
220	structure Scheme.LocalEquations (X : Scheme.{u}) : Type u where
221	  cover : X.PointedCover
222	  eqn : ∀ x, Γ(X, cover.opens x)
223	  regular : ∀ x, /- eqn x is a nonzerodivisor in every stalk over cover.opens x -/
224	  ratio_isUnit : ∀ x y, IsUnit (/- (eqn x)/(eqn y) as a section on the overlap, i.e.
225	      ∃ u : unit on 𝒰x ⊓ 𝒰y, (eqn x)|∩ = u * (eqn y)|∩ -/)
226	
227	def Scheme.LocalEquations.picClass (d : X.LocalEquations) : X.CechPic
228	  -- the class of the cocycle (x,y) ↦ the unit u x y with (eqn x)|∩ = u x y • (eqn y)|∩
229	```
230	
231	with: uniqueness of `u x y` (regularity makes the ratio unit unique — this is why `regular` is
232	part of the data), the cocycle identity for `u` (from associativity of the ratios),
233	*independence*: two `LocalEquations` cutting out the same closed subscheme (or related by
234	unitwise rescaling) have equal `picClass`; *multiplicativity*: pointwise product of equations ↦
235	product of classes; *pullback compatibility*: for `f : X' ⟶ X` such that the pulled-back
236	equations are still regular (guaranteed in the relative situation below),
237	`(d.pullback f).picClass = CechPic.map f d.picClass`.
238	
239	**(b) The two geometric instances** (`Picard/GraphDivisor.lean`):
240	
241	- *Point divisor.* For a `k`-point `P : 𝟙_ (Over (Spec (.of k))) ⟶ C`, the image of `P` is an
242	  effective Cartier divisor on `C.left`: the local ring at the image point is a DVR
243	  (`Curve/StalksDVR.lean`, Wave 1), so a uniformizer spreads to a local equation, and away from
244	  the point the equation `1` works. Output: `pointDivisor P : C.left.LocalEquations` (cover:
245	  a distinguished pointed cover; the choice of uniformizer is data *inside* the construction,
246	  with `picClass`-level independence proven — see the choice-discipline note in §4.4).
247	- *Graph divisor.* The diagonal `Δ ⊂ (C ⊗ C).left` is a relative effective divisor over the
248	  **second** factor: `pr₂|Δ` is an isomorphism onto the base, in particular finite flat of rank
249	  1, and smoothness of `C/k` of relative dimension 1 makes the conormal module invertible, so
250	  the ideal of `Δ` is locally one regular equation. Deliverable:
251	
252	  ```lean
253	  def graphLocalEquations (t : T ⟶ C /- in Over (Spec k) -/) :
254	      ((C ⊗ T).left).LocalEquations   -- local equations for Γ_t := (C ◁ t)-pullback of Δ ⋯
255	  theorem graphLocalEquations_base_change ⋯  -- Γ_{t ∘ g} equations = pullback of Γ_t equations
256	  ```
257	
258	  The base-change stability is *by construction*: `Γ_t` is the pullback of the universal `Δ`
259	  along `C ◁ (t ≫ ⋯)`, and (a)'s pullback compatibility applies because `Δ` is a *relative*
260	  divisor over the test factor (fibers never contain a component of `C`), so regularity
261	  survives every base change. Rank certificate: `𝒪_{Γ_t} ≅ 𝒪_T` as `T`-algebras, so the
262	  finite-flat rank of `Γ_t → T` is 1 — the input for the degree of `abelElement` (§6).
263	  This mathematics is Kleiman `ex:DivC` (§3.8: `X₀ = Div¹_{X/S}` for the smooth locus) and
264	  `rmk:Jac` (§5.26: "Given `t : T → X`, its graph subscheme `Γ_t ⊂ X × T` is a relative
265	  effective divisor"); both read.
266	
267	**(c) The meromorphic bridge** (`Picard/MeromorphicTrivialization.lean`; needed by the degree,
268	see §6.1): for `X` *integral*, every `CechPic` class is a divisor class. Cocycle proof shape:
269	every nonempty open contains the generic point; fix a base index `x₀` and localize the cocycle
270	values `g x x₀` into the function field; these are meromorphic local equations for a Cartier
271	divisor whose class is the given one. (Classical statement: Kleiman quotes it in the proof of
272	`th:qpp&p` (§5.4): "Since `X × T` is integral, there is a divisor `D` such that `𝒪(D) = 𝓛`
273	by [Hartshorne, Ex. II 6.15]".) This file also pins `divisorClass` for *differences*
274	`D₁ − D₂` of effective data as `picClass D₁ * (picClass D₂)⁻¹`.
275	
276	---
277	
278	## 3. (B) The relative functor
279	
280	Recon lesson 3 is binding: the **certified false-axiom trap** (inbox I-0061) is wiring anything
281	to the absolute `Pic(C ×ₖ T)`; the honest functor is the H_T-coset quotient — Kleiman
282	`df:Pfs` (§2.2): "`Pic_{X/S}(T) := Pic(X_T)/Pic(T)`". Kleiman's `df:aPf` discussion (§2.1,
283	read) is the semantic audit anchor for *why* the absolute functor "is never representable".
284	
285	```lean
286	variable (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
287	
288	/-- The relative Picard group of `C/k` at a test object `T`: line-bundle classes on `C ⊗ T`
289	modulo classes pulled back from `T`. -/
290	def relPic (T : Over (Spec (.of k))) : Type u :=
291	  (C ⊗ T).left.CechPic ⧸ (Scheme.CechPic.map (CartesianMonoidalCategory.snd C T).left).range
292	-- CommGroup instance: QuotientGroup on the CommGroup of §2.3.
293	
294	/-- The relative Picard functor. -/
295	def relPicFunctor : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ ⥤ CommGrpCat.{u}
296	```
297	
298	- **Exact quotient relation**: `[L] = [L']` in `relPic T` iff
299	  `L * L'⁻¹ ∈ (CechPic.map (snd C T).left).range` — i.e. iff `L ≅ L' ⊗ pr_T^* N` for some class
300	  `N` on `T`, which in the cocycle model is literally a range condition; no `Nonempty (≅)`
301	  propositions anywhere.
302	- **Evaluation and restriction.** For `g : T' ⟶ T` in `Over (Spec (.of k))`, the map
303	  `relPicFunctor.map g.op` is descent of `CechPic.map ((C ◁ g).left)` to the quotients;
304	  well-defined by the monoidal naturality `(C ◁ g) ≫ snd C T = snd C T' ≫ g`. Functor laws
305	  from `CechPic.map_id/map_comp` plus `QuotientGroup.map` functoriality.
306	- **Universe target**: `CommGrpCat.{u}`, per §1. The functor category
307	  `(Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ ⥤ CommGrpCat.{u}` is legitimate (`Over (Spec k) : Type (u+1)` with
308	  `Type u` homs, `CommGrpCat.{u} : Type (u+1)` with `Type u` homs).
309	- Also provided here (consumed by §4 and Wave 7): naturality in the curve,
310	  `relPicMapCurve (g : C' ⟶ C) : relPicFunctor C ⟶ relPicFunctor C'` (pullback along
311	  `g ▷ T`), strictly functorial in `g`; and the statement of the **base-field shuffle**: for
312	  `L/k` and `T' : Over (Spec (.of L))`, a canonical iso
313	  `relPic (C_L) T' ≃* relPic C ((Over.map (Spec.map _)).obj T')` induced by the scheme
314	  isomorphism `(C_L ⊗_L T').left ≅ (C ⊗_k T'ₖ).left` (`pullbackAssoc`-type; the survey's
315	  `AlgebraicGeometry/Pullbacks.lean` toolkit), compatible with the H-quotients on both sides.
316	
317	---
318	
319	## 4. (C) Étale sheafification, concretely
320

355	### 4.2 The three options, weighed
356	
357	**(i) Hand-rolled plus-construction.** Define
358	`PicEt(T) := colim_{étale covers T'→T} ker(relPic T' ⇉ relPic (T' ×_T T'))` (equalizer form —
359	the plus needs no triple-overlap condition). One plus yields a sheaf iff the input presheaf is
360	separated; `relPic` **is** étale- (even fppf-) separated by Kleiman 2.5(1), whose hypothesis
361	holds by `ex:gc&r`. Cost: the separatedness proof (a genuine descent argument, §4.4), cover
362	smallness/indexing, colimit plumbing. Benefit: construction-canonical, evaluates concretely,
363	`relPic → PicEt` is a unit map usable everywhere, and over test schemes where a section exists
364	the unit is bijective *as a theorem* (2.5(2) recast) — exactly what Wave 4 needs over `k'`.
365	
366	**(ii) Define `PicEt` only via 2.5-comparison where sections exist + descent data elsewhere.**
367	Rejected. A piecewise definition is either non-canonical (it depends on which case a test
368	scheme falls into, and for `baseChangeIso` the case-split differs between `C/k` and `C_L/L`)
369	or secretly equal to (i) with the plus spelled out by hand. Every interface (group law, degree,
370	functoriality in `C`, base-field shuffle) would need case-coherence lemmas. The *content* of
371	(ii) — the comparison bijections — survives as the pair of theorems (C1), (C2) in §4.4.
372	
373	**(iii) Representability over `k'` + Galois descent, with `PicEt := the functor J represents`.**
374	Rejected **as a definition**, retained **as the Wave-4 proof strategy**. The blocker is
375	exactly the one the route anticipates: `baseChangeIso` must compare `(J_C)_L` with `J_{C_L}`,
376	and both must be recognized as representing *the same construction-canonical functor* over `L`.
377	If `PicEt_k` is defined as `Hom(−, J)`, the `RepresentableBy` datum is a tautology carrying no
378	information, and the comparison of `(J_C)_L` with `J_{C_L}` has no common third functor to
379	factor through — one would have to smuggle the construction back in, per-instance, at every
380	coherence. **Resolution (binding):** the functor is defined by construction (option (i)); the
381	`k'`-plus-descent argument is how Wave 4 *produces* the `RepresentableBy` datum; after Wave 4,
382	nothing downstream ever unfolds `J`, only the datum.

384	### 4.3 The decision, in two layers
385	
386	**Layer 1 — affine tests, presented covers** (`Picard/EtaleCovers.lean`, `Picard/PicEtAff.lean`).
387	
388	For `T` with `T.left` affine (`A := Γ(T.left, ⊤)`), an étale cover index is a *presentation*:
389	
390	```lean
391	/-- A presented affine étale cover of `Spec A`: a chosen finite presentation of an étale,
392	faithfully flat `A`-algebra. -/
393	structure EtCover (A : CommRingCat.{u}) : Type u where
394	  n m : ℕ
395	  relations : Fin m → MvPolynomial (Fin n) A
396	  -- carrier B := (MvPolynomial (Fin n) A) ⧸ (span of relations)
397	  etale : Algebra.Etale A B
398	  surjective : /- Spec B → Spec A surjective (with étale + fp this gives faithful flatness) -/
399	```
400	
401	- `Type u`-small by construction, choice-free, and closed under the operations the plus needs:
402	  a *refinement* of covers is a `T`-morphism `Spec B' → Spec B`; *directedness* via
403	  `B ⊗[A] B'` (which has an explicit presentation); *base change* along `A → A'` re-presents
404	  with the same polynomials.
405	- Descent classes and the one-step plus, equalizer form:
406	
407	```lean
408	def descentClasses (E : EtCover A) : Subgroup (relPic C (T' E)) :=
409	  -- ker of (pullback along pr₁) / (pullback along pr₂) into relPic C (T' E ⊗_T T' E)
410	def PicEtAff (T /- affine -/) : Type u :=
411	  -- Σ (E : EtCover A), descentClasses E, quotiented by refinement, CommGroup
412	def picEtAffUnit : relPic C T →* PicEtAff C T   -- classes with the tautological descent datum
413	```
414	
415	- *Refinement-map independence* (the lemma that makes the colimit canonical): two `T`-morphisms
416	  `h₁ h₂ : Spec B'' → Spec B'` induce the same map on `descentClasses`, because
417	  `(h₁, h₂) : Spec B'' → Spec B' ×_T Spec B'` pulls the descent-datum equation
418	  `p₁^*λ = p₂^*λ` back to `h₁^*λ = h₂^*λ`. One line, but it is the keystone of
419	  well-definedness; pin it as a named lemma.
420	- Zariski refinements are included automatically: a standard affine cover
421	  `Spec (∏ᵢ A_{fᵢ}) → Spec A` is a presented étale cover, so the plus also performs the
422	  Zariski sheafification on affines — needed for `relPic`-vs-`PicEt` comparisons to be honest.
423	- Over a *field* base `Spec K`, single-factor refinement works (any factor field of an étale
424	  `K`-algebra already covers the point), so **field-extension covers are cofinal** — pin this
425	  lemma; it makes `PicEtAff C (Spec K) = colim_{K'/K fin. sep.} (Galois-stable part of
426	  relPic over K')`, the form the degree (§6) and Wave 4 consume.
427	
428	**Layer 2 — all test objects** (`Picard/PicEt.lean`).
429	
430	`GrpObj.ofRepresentableBy` forces the functor to be defined on **all** of `Over (Spec (.of k))`
431	(the frozen `instGrpObj` leaves no choice), while the plus is only well-behaved on affines. The
432	extension is the canonical right-Kan-style limit over affine opens:
433	
434	```lean
435	def picEt (T : Over (Spec (.of k))) : Type u :=
436	  -- lim over the poset of affine opens U ≤ T.left of PicEtAff C (T restricted to U),
437	  -- i.e. compatible families (λ_U)_U; CommGroup pointwise
438	def picEtFunctor : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ ⥤ CommGrpCat.{u}
439	def picEtUnit : relPicFunctor C ⟶ picEtFunctor C
440	theorem picEt_affine_iso (hT : IsAffine T.left) : picEt C T ≃* PicEtAff C T ⋯
441	```
442	
443	For affine `T`, `T.left` is the top of its own affine-opens poset, so the limit collapses to
444	`PicEtAff C T` (canonical iso, not defeq — one lemma). Functoriality in `T` maps a family
445	`(λ_V)_V` over `T` to the family `(res λ_V)` indexed by pairs `U ⊆ f⁻¹V` — the comma-limit
446	construction. `picEt` is a Zariski sheaf by construction; the étale sheaf sequence is claimed
447	(and needed) **only for affine `T` with presented covers** — this is recorded as the honest
448	semantic pin in the blueprint: "`picEtFunctor` restricted to affine tests *is* the étale
449	sheafification of `relPicFunctor` there (one plus of a separated presheaf), and is its canonical
450	Zariski-continuous extension elsewhere." **OPEN-1**: whether Layer 2 is implemented as this
451	bespoke limit or through mathlib's dense-subsite machinery
452	(`AlgebraicGeometry/Sites/Affine.lean`: `isCoverDense_toOver_Spec` + `IsCoverDense` sheaf
453	extension); closing criterion in §9.
454	
455	Also in `Picard/PicEt.lean`, stated at this level because Wave 7 consumes them:
456	
457	- `picEtMapCurve (g : C' ⟶ C) : picEtFunctor C ⟶ picEtFunctor C'` with `mapCurve_id/comp`
458	  (descend `relPicMapCurve` through the plus and the limit; pullback preserves descent data).
459	- The **base-field shuffle**, étale level: for `L/k` and `T' : Over (Spec (.of L))`,
460	  `picEtBaseField : picEt (C_L) T' ≃* picEt C (T'ₖ)` — descends from §3's `relPic` shuffle
461	  because an étale cover of `T'` is *the same thing* over `L` and over `k` (étaleness and
462	  presentations are `T'`-intrinsic; this is precisely why the plus is indexed by covers **of
463	  the test scheme**, never of the base). Natural in `T'`, compatible with units and with
464	  `picEtMapCurve`.

466	### 4.4 Why one plus suffices: the separatedness ledger
467	
468	**(C1) Separatedness** (`Picard/Separatedness.lean`): for affine `T` and a presented étale
469	cover `E`, the map `relPic C T → relPic C (T' E)` is injective. This is Kleiman 2.5(1)
470	restricted to what we consume, recast on cocycles. Proof ledger (all pieces named because they
471	are shared bricks):
472	
473	1. `sectionsBaseChange` (`Cohomology/SectionsBaseChange.lean`): for `V ⊆ C.left` affine open
474	   and a `k`-algebra `A`, `Γ((C ⊗ Spec A).left, V_A) ≅ Γ(C.left, V) ⊗[k] A`, naturally.
475	   *Shared with*: the T₀ dual-numbers engine (`A = k[ε]`, recon lesson 7) and the χ-ledger over
476	   field extensions (`A = K`). One brick, three consumers.
477	2. `universalSections` (`Picard/UniversalSections.lean`): `Γ((C ⊗ Spec A).left, ⊤) = A` for
478	   every `k`-algebra `A` — the two-cover H⁰ slice: the complex
479	   `Γ(V₀) ⊕ Γ(V₁) → Γ(V₀ ⊓ V₁)` has `H⁰ = k` (Wave 1), stays exact under the flat `⊗[k] A`
480	   by 1. This is our discharge of Kleiman's `ex:gc&r` hypothesis in the form actually consumed.
481	3. `prPullback_injective`: `CechPic.map (snd C T).left` is injective for affine `T` — a unit
482	   cocycle on `C ⊗ T` trivializing must have come from `T`, because
483	   `𝒪ˣ((C ⊗ V).left) = Γ(V)ˣ` by 2 (applied on an affine pointed cover of `T`). Hence the
484	   H_T-quotient loses nothing it shouldn't, and "which `N`" in a `pr^*N`-equation is unique.
485	4. `Descent/InvertibleModule.lean` (pure algebra, PR-candidate): along a faithfully flat ring
486	   map `A → B`, an invertible `B`-module with a descent datum descends to an invertible
487	   `A`-module, uniquely up to canonical isomorphism. (Survey: this exists **nowhere** in
488	   mathlib — "no effective descent of modules"; it is the honest algebraic core of both (C1)
489	   and (C2).)
490	5. Assembly (Kleiman's 2.5(1) argument recast): a class `λ ∈ relPic C T` dying on the cover
491	   gives, via 3 applied over `T'` and `T' ×_T T'`, a line-bundle class `n'` on `T'` with a
492	   descent datum along `Spec B → Spec A`; by 4 it descends to `n` on `T`, and `λ = pr^* n`
493	   follows from 3 again. Hence `λ = 0` in the quotient.

7	/-!
8	# Global sections of a proper geometrically integral scheme over a field
9	
10	The keystone of the curve substrate: for a scheme `X` proper and geometrically integral over a
11	field `K`, the structure map induces an isomorphism `K ≅ Γ(X, 𝒪_X)`.
12	
13	* `AlgebraicGeometry.bijective_appTop_of_isProper_of_geometricallyIntegral`:
14	  the honest general form — `f.appTop : Γ(Spec K, ⊤) ⟶ Γ(X, ⊤)` is bijective.
15	* `AlgebraicGeometry.isIso_appTop_of_isProper_of_geometricallyIntegral` and the bundle instance
16	  `AlgebraicGeometry.isIso_hom_appTop_of_geometricallyReduced`: the instance-friendly forms.
17	
18	## Proof sketch
19	
20	Write `A := Γ(X, ⊤)`. By Mathlib's properness facts (`isField_of_universallyClosed`,
21	`finite_appTop_of_universallyClosed`), `A` is a field, finite over `K`. Base change `f` along
22	`Spec A ⟶ Spec K`: the total space `X_A` is again proper and geometrically integral over the
23	field `A`, so `Γ(X_A, ⊤)` is a field as well. Flat base change of sections
24	(`isIso_pushoutSection_of_isQuasiSeparated_of_flat_right`) exhibits `Γ(X_A, ⊤)` as the pushout
25	`A ⊗[K] A`. A pushout of a field extension along itself being a field forces `K ⟶ A` to be an
26	*epimorphism* of rings (`CommRingCat.epi_of_isPushout_of_isField`: the codiagonal
27	`A ⊗[K] A ⟶ A` is injective, being a ring map out of a field, and surjective, being split by
28	`inl`; hence `inl` is an isomorphism and the two coprojections agree). A finite ring
29	epimorphism is surjective (`RingHom.surjective_of_epi_of_finite`), and any ring map out of a
30	field is injective.
31	
32	Geometric reducedness enters only through `GeometricallyIntegral`; for the curve bundle of the
33	challenge it is supplied by "smooth ⟹ geometrically reduced", proved elsewhere in this project.
34	-/
35	
36	set_option autoImplicit false
37	
38	universe u
39	
40	open CategoryTheory Limits
41	
42	namespace CommRingCat
43	
44	/-- If a pushout square of commutative rings has isomorphic legs (`e : C ≅ B` intertwining
45	`ψ` and `φ`) and its pushout `D` is a field, then `φ` is an epimorphism.
46	
47	This is the classical "diagonal" criterion: the codiagonal `μ : D ⟶ B` determined by
48	`𝟙 B` and `e.hom` is injective (a ring map out of a field into a nontrivial ring) and split
49	surjective, hence an isomorphism; so `inl = e.inv ≫ inr`, which makes `φ` epi. -/
50	lemma epi_of_isPushout_of_isField {A B C D : CommRingCat.{u}}
51	    {φ : A ⟶ B} {ψ : A ⟶ C} {inl : B ⟶ D} {inr : C ⟶ D}
52	    (H : IsPushout φ ψ inl inr) (hD : IsField D) [Nontrivial B]
53	    (e : C ≅ B) (he : ψ ≫ e.hom = φ) : Epi φ := by
54	  letI : Field D := hD.toField
55	  -- the codiagonal
56	  let μ : D ⟶ B := H.desc (𝟙 B) e.hom (by rw [Category.comp_id, he])
57	  have hμinl : inl ≫ μ = 𝟙 B := H.inl_desc _ _ _
58	  have hμinr : inr ≫ μ = e.hom := H.inr_desc _ _ _
59	  have : IsIso μ := by
60	    refine (ConcreteCategory.isIso_iff_bijective μ).mpr ⟨μ.hom.injective, fun b ↦ ⟨inl b, ?_⟩⟩
61	    simpa using congr($(hμinl) b)
62	  -- the two coprojections agree up to `e`
63	  have key : e.inv ≫ inr = inl := by
64	    rw [← cancel_mono μ, Category.assoc, hμinr, hμinl, Iso.inv_hom_id]
65	  refine ⟨fun {W} u v huv ↦ ?_⟩
66	  have w : φ ≫ u = ψ ≫ (e.hom ≫ v) := by
67	    rw [← Category.assoc, he]; exact huv
68	  calc u = inl ≫ H.desc u (e.hom ≫ v) w := (H.inl_desc _ _ _).symm
69	    _ = e.inv ≫ inr ≫ H.desc u (e.hom ≫ v) w := by rw [← Category.assoc, key]
70	    _ = e.inv ≫ e.hom ≫ v := by rw [H.inr_desc]
71	    _ = v := by rw [Iso.inv_hom_id_assoc]
72	
73	end CommRingCat
74	
75	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
76	
77	/-- Bundled variant of `AlgebraicGeometry.isField_of_universallyClosed`: if `X` is an integral
78	scheme, universally closed over the spectrum of a (bundled) commutative ring `R` that is a
79	field, then `Γ(X, ⊤)` is a field. -/
80	theorem isField_of_universallyClosed_of_isField {R : CommRingCat.{u}} (hR : IsField R)
81	    {X : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Spec R) [IsIntegral X] [UniversallyClosed f] :
82	    IsField Γ(X, ⊤) := by
83	  let F := (Scheme.ΓSpecIso R).inv ≫ f.appTop
84	  have : F.hom.IsIntegral := by
85	    apply RingHom.isIntegral_respectsIso.2 (e := (Scheme.ΓSpecIso R).symm.commRingCatIsoToRingEquiv)
86	    exact isIntegral_appTop_of_universallyClosed f
87	  algebraize [F.hom]
88	  exact isField_of_isIntegral_of_isField' hR
89	
90	/-- **Global sections of a proper geometrically integral scheme over a field.**
91	If `X` is proper and geometrically integral over a field `K`, then the map on global sections
92	`Γ(Spec K, ⊤) ⟶ Γ(X, ⊤)` induced by the structure morphism is bijective; informally,
93	`Γ(X, 𝒪_X) = K`. -/
94	theorem bijective_appTop_of_isProper_of_geometricallyIntegral
95	    {K : Type u} [Field K] {X : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of K))
96	    [IsProper f] [GeometricallyIntegral f] :
97	    Function.Bijective f.appTop := by
98	  have hX : IsIntegral X := GeometricallyIntegral.isIntegral_of_subsingleton f
99	  -- `A := Γ(X, ⊤)` is a field, finite over `K`.
100	  have hA : IsField Γ(X, ⊤) := isField_of_universallyClosed K f
101	  letI : Field Γ(X, ⊤) := hA.toField
102	  letI : Field Γ(Spec (CommRingCat.of K), ⊤) :=
103	    ((Scheme.ΓSpecIso (CommRingCat.of K)).commRingCatIsoToRingEquiv.toMulEquiv.isField
104	      (Field.toIsField K)).toField
105	  refine ⟨f.appTop.hom.injective, ?_⟩
106	  -- Surjectivity: `f.appTop` is a finite epimorphism.
107	  suffices h : Epi f.appTop from
108	    RingHom.surjective_of_epi_of_finite f.appTop (finite_appTop_of_universallyClosed K f)
109	  -- Base change to `Spec Γ(X, ⊤)`.
110	  set q : Spec Γ(X, ⊤) ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of K) :=
111	    Spec.map ((Scheme.ΓSpecIso (CommRingCat.of K)).inv ≫ f.appTop) with hq
112	  -- The total space of the base change is integral, so its global sections form a field.
113	  have hsub : Subsingleton ↥(Spec Γ(X, ⊤)) :=
114	    inferInstanceAs (Subsingleton (PrimeSpectrum Γ(X, ⊤)))
115	  have hYint : IsIntegral (pullback f q) :=
116	    GeometricallyIntegral.isIntegral_of_subsingleton (pullback.snd f q)
117	  have hUC : UniversallyClosed (pullback.snd f q) :=
118	    MorphismProperty.pullback_snd _ _ inferInstance
119	  have hD : IsField Γ(pullback f q, ⊤) :=
120	    isField_of_universallyClosed_of_isField hA (pullback.snd f q)
121	  -- Flat base change of global sections: the pushout square.
122	  have hUST : (⊤ : (Spec Γ(X, ⊤)).Opens) ≤ q ⁻¹ᵁ ⊤ := (Scheme.Hom.preimage_top q).ge
123	  have hUSX : (⊤ : X.Opens) ≤ f ⁻¹ᵁ ⊤ := (Scheme.Hom.preimage_top f).ge
124	  have hUY : (⊤ : (pullback f q).Opens) =
125	      pullback.fst f q ⁻¹ᵁ ⊤ ⊓ pullback.snd f q ⁻¹ᵁ ⊤ := by simp
126	  have hCS : CompactSpace X := QuasiCompact.compactSpace_of_compactSpace f
127	  have hQS : QuasiSeparatedSpace X := quasiSeparatedSpace_of_quasiSeparated f
128	  have hiso := isIso_pushoutSection_of_isQuasiSeparated_of_flat_right
129	    (IsPullback.of_hasPullback f q) hUST hUSX hUY
130	    (isAffineOpen_top _) (isAffineOpen_top _)
131	    (by simpa using CompactSpace.isCompact_univ)
132	    (by simpa using isQuasiSeparated_univ)
133	  have hpo := (isIso_pushoutSection_iff
134	    (IsPullback.of_hasPullback f q) hUST hUSX hUY).mp hiso
135	  -- The two legs of the pushout square agree up to `ΓSpecIso`.
136	  have hcompat : q.appLE ⊤ ⊤ hUST ≫ (Scheme.ΓSpecIso Γ(X, ⊤)).hom = f.appLE ⊤ ⊤ hUSX := by
137	    have h₁ : q.appLE ⊤ ⊤ hUST = q.appTop := Scheme.Hom.appLE_eq_app q
138	    have h₂ : f.appLE ⊤ ⊤ hUSX = f.appTop := Scheme.Hom.appLE_eq_app f
139	    rw [h₁, h₂, hq, Scheme.ΓSpecIso_naturality, Iso.hom_inv_id_assoc]
140	  have hepi : Epi (f.appLE ⊤ ⊤ hUSX) :=
141	    CommRingCat.epi_of_isPushout_of_isField hpo hD (Scheme.ΓSpecIso Γ(X, ⊤)) hcompat
142	  rwa [show f.appLE ⊤ ⊤ hUSX = f.appTop from Scheme.Hom.appLE_eq_app f] at hepi
143	
144	/-- Instance-friendly form of
145	`AlgebraicGeometry.bijective_appTop_of_isProper_of_geometricallyIntegral`. -/
146	theorem isIso_appTop_of_isProper_of_geometricallyIntegral
147	    {K : Type u} [Field K] {X : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of K))
148	    [IsProper f] [GeometricallyIntegral f] :
149	    IsIso f.appTop :=
150	  (ConcreteCategory.isIso_iff_bijective _).mpr
151	    (bijective_appTop_of_isProper_of_geometricallyIntegral f)
152	
153	variable {k : Type u} [Field k]
154	
155	/-- `Γ(C, 𝒪_C) ≅ k` for the curve bundle: the structure morphism of a proper, geometrically
156	irreducible, geometrically reduced scheme over `k` induces an isomorphism on global sections.
157	
158	Geometric reducedness is a hypothesis here; for the curve bundle of the challenge it is
159	supplied by "smooth ⟹ geometrically reduced", proved elsewhere in this project. -/
160	instance isIso_hom_appTop_of_geometricallyReduced (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
161	    [IsProper C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom] [GeometricallyReduced C.hom] :
162	    IsIso C.hom.appTop :=
163	  have : GeometricallyIntegral C.hom :=
164	    GeometricallyIntegral.of_geometricallyReduced_of_geometricallyIrreducible C.hom
165	  isIso_appTop_of_isProper_of_geometricallyIntegral (K := k) C.hom
166	
167	section RegressionChecks
168	
169	variable {C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))}
170	  [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
171	  [GeometricallyReduced C.hom]
172	
173	-- The composite `k ≅ Γ(Spec k, ⊤) ≅ Γ(C, 𝒪_C)` is available to downstream waves.
174	noncomputable example : CommRingCat.of k ≅ Γ(C.left, ⊤) :=
175	  (Scheme.ΓSpecIso (CommRingCat.of k)).symm ≪≫ asIso C.hom.appTop
176	
177	end RegressionChecks
178	
179	end AlgebraicGeometry

186	## Sections of fibered products

188	Suppose we are given the following cartesian square:

198	
199	We show that this map is
200	1. `isIso_pushoutSection_of_isAffineOpen`:
201	  bijective when `Uₛ`, `Uₜ`, and `Uₓ` are all affine.

203	  injective when `Uₛ`, `Uₜ` are affine, `Uₓ` is compact, and `f` is flat.

255	  /-
256	  We shall show that `Γ(T, Uₜ) ⊗[Γ(S, Uₛ)] Γ(X, U) ⟶ Γ(X ×ₛ T, pr₁ ⁻¹ U ∩ pr₂ ⁻¹ Uₜ)` is
257	  injective using the following diagram
258	  ```
259	  Γ(T, Uₜ) ⊗ Γ(X, U) ------→ Γ(T, Uₜ) ⊗ ∏ᵢ Γ(X, Vᵢ)
260	           |                          |
261	           ↓                          ↓
262	  Γ(X ×ₛ T, U ∩ Uₜ)  ------→ ∏ᵢ Γ(X ×ₛ T, Vᵢ ∩ Uₜ)
263	  ```
264	  -/
265	  have (i : _) : VX i ≤ iX ⁻¹ᵁ US := by clear hV; aesop
266	  classical
267	  algebraize [(iX.appLE US UX hUSX).hom, (f.appLE US UT hUST).hom]
268	  let (i : _) := (iX.appLE US (VX i) (by aesop)).hom.toAlgebra
269	  -- This is the map `Γ(X ×ₛ T, U ∩ Uₜ) ⟶ ∏ᵢ Γ(X ×ₛ T, Vᵢ ∩ Uₜ)` on the bottom.
270	  let ψY : Γ(Y, UY) →+* Π i, Γ(Y, g ⁻¹ᵁ VX i ⊓ iY ⁻¹ᵁ UT) := RingHom.pi fun i ↦
271	      (Y.presheaf.map (homOfLE (by subst hUY hVU; gcongr; exact le_iSup _ _)).op).hom
272	  -- The map `Γ(X, U) ⟶ ∏ᵢ Γ(X, Vᵢ)`
273	  let ψ : Γ(X, UX) →ₐ[Γ(S, US)] Π i, Γ(X, VX i) := Pi.algHom _ _ fun i ↦
274	    ⟨(X.presheaf.map (homOfLE (hVU ▸ le_iSup VX i)).op).hom, fun r ↦ by
275	      dsimp [RingHom.algebraMap_toAlgebra]
276	      simp only [← CommRingCat.comp_apply, Scheme.Hom.appLE_map]⟩
277	  -- ... is injective by the sheaf axiom,
278	  have hψ : Function.Injective ψ := by
279	    intro s t est
280	    apply X.IsSheaf.section_ext fun x hx ↦ ?_
281	    simp only [← hVU, Opens.mem_iSup] at hx
282	    obtain ⟨i, hxi⟩ := hx
283	    exact ⟨_, _, hxi, congr($est i)⟩
284	  -- ... and remains injective after tensoring with `Γ(T, Uₜ)` by the flatness assumption.
285	  have hψ' : Function.Injective (Algebra.TensorProduct.map (AlgHom.id Γ(T, UT) Γ(T, UT)) ψ) :=
286	    Module.Flat.lTensor_preserves_injective_linearMap ψ.toLinearMap hψ
287	  simp_rw [@ConcreteCategory.mono_iff_injective_of_preservesPullback] at hV ⊢
288	  cases nonempty_fintype ι
289	  -- And the map at the right
290	  let φ : (Γ(T, UT) ⊗[Γ(S, US)] Π i, Γ(X, VX i)) →+* Π i, Γ(Y, g ⁻¹ᵁ VX i ⊓ iY ⁻¹ᵁ UT) :=
291	    (RingHom.pi fun i ↦ (pushoutSection H hUST (show VX i ≤ _ by aesop) rfl).hom.comp
292	      ((CommRingCat.isPushout_tensorProduct _ _ _).flip.isoPushout.hom.hom.comp
293	      (by exact Pi.evalRingHom _ _))).comp (Algebra.TensorProduct.piRight _ Γ(S, US) _ _).toRingHom
294	  -- ... is also injective by our hypotheses on `Vᵢ`.
295	  have hφ : Function.Injective φ := by
296	    dsimp [φ]
297	    refine .comp ?_ (Algebra.TensorProduct.piRight _ Γ(S, US) _ _).injective
298	    exact .piMap fun i ↦ (hV _).comp <| CommRingCat.isPushout_tensorProduct _ _ _
299	      |>.flip.isoPushout.commRingCatIsoToRingEquiv.injective
300	  let e : pushout (iX.appLE US UX hUSX) (f.appLE US UT hUST) ≅
301	      .of (Γ(T, UT) ⊗[Γ(S, US)] Γ(X, UX)) :=
302	    (CommRingCat.isPushout_tensorProduct _ _ _).flip.isoPushout.symm
303	  -- It remains to check that the square indeed commutes, and we may conclude that the map
304	  -- at the left is also injective.
305	  suffices (ψY.comp (pushoutSection H hUST hUSX hUY).hom).comp e.inv.hom = φ.comp
306	      (Algebra.TensorProduct.map (AlgHom.id Γ(T, UT) Γ(T, UT)) ψ).toRingHom by
307	    refine .of_comp (f := ψY) ?_
308	    convert (hφ.comp hψ').comp e.commRingCatIsoToRingEquiv.injective
309	    ext1 x; simpa using! congr($this (e.hom x))
310	  ext1
311	  · have H₁ : e.inv.hom.comp Algebra.TensorProduct.includeLeftRingHom =
312	        (pushout.inr (C := CommRingCat) _ _).hom :=
313	      congr($((CommRingCat.isPushout_tensorProduct _ _ _).flip.inr_isoPushout_hom).hom)
314	    have H₂ (x j) : φ (x ⊗ₜ[↑Γ(S, US)] 1) j = pushoutSection H hUST (UX := VX j) (by simp_all) rfl
315	        (pushout.inr (C := CommRingCat) _ _ x) := congr(pushoutSection H hUST (UX := VX j) _ rfl
316	        ($((CommRingCat.isPushout_tensorProduct ↑Γ(S, US)
317	          ↑Γ(T, UT) ↑Γ(X, VX j)).flip.inr_isoPushout_hom) x))
318	    simp only [RingHom.comp_assoc, H₁]
319	    ext x j
320	    simp [ψY, H₂, ← CategoryTheory.comp_apply, pushoutSection]
321	  · have H₁ : e.inv.hom.comp Algebra.TensorProduct.includeRight.toRingHom =
322	        (pushout.inl (C := CommRingCat) _ _).hom :=
323	      congr($((CommRingCat.isPushout_tensorProduct _ _ _).flip.inl_isoPushout_hom).hom)
324	    have H₂ (x j) : φ (1 ⊗ₜ[↑Γ(S, US)] x) j = pushoutSection H hUST (UX := VX j) (by simp_all) rfl
325	        (pushout.inl (C := CommRingCat) _ _ (x j)) := congr(pushoutSection H hUST (UX := VX j) _ rfl
326	        ($((CommRingCat.isPushout_tensorProduct ↑Γ(S, US)
327	          ↑Γ(T, UT) ↑Γ(X, VX j)).flip.inl_isoPushout_hom) (x j)))
328	    simp only [RingHom.comp_assoc, H₁]
329	    ext x j
330	    simp [ψY, H₂, -CommRingCat.hom_comp, ← CategoryTheory.comp_apply, pushoutSection, ψ]

338	      (show VX i ⊓ VX j ≤ _ from inf_le_left.trans (by clear hV; aesop)) rfl))
339	    (hT : (f.appLE US UT hUST).hom.Flat) :
340	    IsIso (pushoutSection H hUST hUSX hUY) := by
341	  classical
342	  /-
343	  We shall show that `Γ(T, Uₜ) ⊗[Γ(S, Uₛ)] Γ(X, U) ⟶ Γ(X ×ₛ T, pr₁ ⁻¹ U ∩ pr₂ ⁻¹ Uₜ)` is
344	  injective using the following diagram
345	  ```
346	  0 → Γ(T, Uₜ) ⊗ Γ(X, U) ------→ Γ(T, Uₜ) ⊗ ∏ᵢ Γ(X, Vᵢ) ---→ Γ(T, Uₜ) ⊗ ∏ᵢⱼ Γ(X, Vᵢ ∩ Vⱼ)
347	           |                              |                           |
348	           ↓                              ↓                           ↓
349	  0 → Γ(X ×ₛ T, U ∩ Uₜ)  ------→ ∏ᵢ Γ(X ×ₛ T, Vᵢ ∩ Uₜ)  ---→ ∏ᵢ Γ(X ×ₛ T, Vᵢ ∩ Vⱼ ∩ Uₜ)
350	  ```
351	  The two rows are exact because of the sheaf axiom (and additionally the flatness assumption for
352	  the top row). The vertical arrow in the middle is an isomorphism by assumption, and the one
353	  one the right is monomorphic by assumption. Hence the left arrow is also an isomorphism.
354	
355	  In the actual proof we use `Pairwise`-indexed diagrams instead of nested limits because it works
356	  better with the existing API.
357	  -/
358	  -- The diagram consisting of `Γ(X, Vᵢ) ⟶ Γ(X, Vᵢ ∩ Vⱼ)`.
359	  let D := Pairwise.diagram VX
360	  have h : iSup D.obj = UX := by
361	    refine le_antisymm (iSup_le_iff.mpr ?_) ?_
362	    · subst hVU; rintro (i | ⟨i, j⟩); exacts [le_iSup VX _, inf_le_left.trans (le_iSup VX _)]
363	    · subst hVU; exact iSup_le_iff.mpr fun i ↦ le_iSup D.obj (.single i)
364	  let c₀ : Cocone D := (colimit.cocone _).extend
365	    (eqToIso (Y := UX) (by simpa [CompleteLattice.colimit_eq_iSup])).hom
366	  -- The diagram consisting of `Γ(T, Uₜ) ⊗ Γ(X, Vᵢ) ⟶ Γ(T, Uₜ) ⊗ Γ(X, Vᵢ ∩ Vⱼ)`.
367	  let F := Under.lift _ ((Functor.const _).map (iX.appLE US UX hUSX) ≫
368	    ((X.presheaf.mapCone c₀.op).π)) ⋙ Under.pushout (f.appLE US UT hUST) ⋙ Under.forget _
369	  let G : X.Opens ⥤ Y.Opens :=
370	    { obj U := g ⁻¹ᵁ U ⊓ iY ⁻¹ᵁ UT, map h := homOfLE (by gcongr; exact h.le) }
371	  -- The natural transformation between the diagrams at the top and bottom.
372	  let αF : F ⟶ D.op ⋙ G.op ⋙ Y.presheaf :=
373	  { app i := (pushout.congrHom (by simp) rfl).hom ≫
374	      pushoutSection H hUST (by grw [← hUSX, ← h]; exact le_iSup D.obj i.unop) rfl }
375	  -- `Γ(T, Uₜ) ⊗ Γ(X, U)` as a (limit) cone over the top diagram.
376	  let c : Cone F := (Under.pushout (f.appLE US UT hUST) ⋙ Under.forget _).mapCone
377	    (Under.liftCone (X.presheaf.mapCone c₀.op) _)
378	  have := CommRingCat.Under.preservesFiniteLimits_of_flat _ hT
379	  cases nonempty_fintype ι
380	  let hc : IsLimit c :=
381	    haveI HX := ((TopCat.Presheaf.isSheaf_iff_isSheafPreservesLimitPairwiseIntersections

383	    haveI HX := (HX (IsColimit.extendIso _ (colimit.isColimit _)).op).some
384	    isLimitOfPreserves (Under.pushout _ ⋙ Under.forget _) (Under.isLimitLiftCone _ _ HX)
385	  let c'₀ : Cocone (D ⋙ G) := (colimit.cocone _).extend
386	    (eqToIso (Y := UY) (by
387	      simp only [colimit.cocone_x, CompleteLattice.colimit_eq_iSup]
388	      eta_expand
389	      dsimp [G]
390	      rw [← iSup_inf_eq, ← Scheme.Hom.preimage_iSup, h, hUY])).hom
391	  -- `Γ(X ×ₛ T, U ∩ Uₜ)` as a (limit) cone over the bottom diagram.
392	  let c' : Cone (D.op ⋙ G.op ⋙ Y.presheaf) := Y.presheaf.mapCone c'₀.op

394	    letI e : D ⋙ G ≅ Pairwise.diagram fun i ↦ g ⁻¹ᵁ VX i ⊓ iY ⁻¹ᵁ UT :=

397	    haveI HX := ((TopCat.Presheaf.isSheaf_iff_isSheafPreservesLimitPairwiseIntersections _).mp
398	      Y.IsSheaf (fun i ↦ g ⁻¹ᵁ VX i ⊓ iY ⁻¹ᵁ UT)).preserves
399	        (c := ((Cocone.precompose e.inv).obj c'₀).op)
400	    exact (IsLimit.postcomposeHomEquiv (Functor.isoWhiskerRight (NatIso.op e.symm) Y.presheaf) _)

402	        (IsColimit.extendIso _ (colimit.isColimit _))).op).some.ofIsoLimit (Cone.ext (.refl _)))

406	  let f₂ : c'.pt ⟶ c.pt := hc.lift ⟨c'.pt, ⟨fun
407	    | .op (.single i) => c'.π.app _ ≫ inv (αF.app (.op <| .single i))
408	    | .op (.pair i j) => c'.π.app (.op (.single i)) ≫ inv (αF.app (.op <| .single i)) ≫

410	    rintro ⟨i⟩ ⟨j⟩ f

412	      (show Function.Surjective Quiver.Hom.op from Quiver.Hom.opEquiv.surjective) f
413	    · simp [show Pairwise.Hom.id_single i = 𝟙 (Pairwise.single i) from rfl]
414	    · simp [show Pairwise.Hom.id_pair i j = 𝟙 (Pairwise.pair i j) from rfl]
415	    · simp
416	    · rw [← cancel_mono (αF.app _)]
417	      simpa using (c'.w (Quiver.Hom.op <| Pairwise.Hom.left i j)).trans
418	        (c'.w (Quiver.Hom.op <| Pairwise.Hom.right i j)).symm⟩⟩

420	  let e : c.pt ≅ c'.pt := by
421	    refine ⟨f₁, f₂, hc.hom_ext ?_, hc'.hom_ext ?_⟩
422	    · rintro ⟨i | ⟨i, j⟩⟩ <;> simp [f₁, f₂]
423	    · rintro ⟨i | ⟨i, j⟩⟩
424	      · simp [f₁, f₂]
425	      · simpa [f₁, f₂] using c'.w (Quiver.Hom.op <| Pairwise.Hom.left i j)
426	  convert! e.isIso_hom using 1
427	  · refine hc'.hom_ext fun i ↦ ?_
428	    rw [hc'.fac]
429	    ext1
430	    · simp [αF, c, Under.liftCone, c', c₀]
431	    · simp [αF, c, c']

6	import AlgebraicJacobian.Cohomology.AffineVanishing

8	/-!
9	# The two-affine-cover H¹ cokernel bridge
10	
11	For a scheme `X` over `Spec k` covered by two affine opens `U₀ ⊔ U₁ = ⊤`, this file
12	computes the degree-one cohomology of the structure sheaf (as a sheaf of `k`-modules on
13	the small Zariski site, `Sheaf.HModule`) as an explicit cokernel of a map of section
14	modules:
15	
16	`H¹ₖ(X, 𝒪ₖ) ≃ₗ[k] Γ(X, U₀ ⊓ U₁) ⧸ range((s₀, s₁) ↦ s₀|_{U₀⊓U₁} - s₁|_{U₀⊓U₁})`
17	
18	(`AlgebraicGeometry.TwoCover.h1CokEquiv`, with the cokernel carrier
19	`AlgebraicGeometry.TwoCover.H1Cok`). This is the computational access point for the genus
20	of a curve: `genus C = finrank k H¹ₖ(C, 𝒪_C)` becomes the corank of an explicit map of
21	function spaces.
22	
23	**Hypotheses actually used**: `X` any scheme over `Spec k`, `IsAffineOpen U₀`,
24	`IsAffineOpen U₁`, `U₀ ⊔ U₁ = ⊤`. In particular *no* affineness (or even
25	quasi-compactness) hypothesis on the intersection `U₀ ⊓ U₁` is needed — unlike for the
26	classical Čech-complex identification, the derived-functor Mayer–Vietoris sequence of
27	`AlgebraicJacobian.Cohomology.MayerVietoris` is exact regardless, and affineness of the
28	two pieces alone kills their `H¹'` (`IsAffineOpen.subsingleton_moduleKSheaf_hModule'_one`).
29	
30	## Main declarations
31	
32	* `Scheme.twoCoverSquare` — the Mayer–Vietoris square `(U₀ ⊓ U₁, U₀, U₁, ⊤)` on the
33	  small Zariski site of `X`, for a covering pair of opens.
34	* `Scheme.twoCoverH1LinearEquiv` — the general-coefficients form: for any sheaf `F` of
35	  `k`-modules with `H¹'(U₀, F)` and `H¹'(U₁, F)` subsingletons,
36	  `HModule F 1 ≃ₗ[k] F(U₀ ⊓ U₁) ⧸ range(moduleDiff)` (reusable for twisted sheaves).
37	* `TwoCover.diff k X U₀ U₁` — the difference map `Γ(U₀) × Γ(U₁) →ₗ[k] Γ(U₀ ⊓ U₁)`.
38	* `TwoCover.H1Cok k X U₀ U₁` — the cokernel carrier `Γ(U₀ ⊓ U₁) ⧸ range diff`.
39	* `TwoCover.delta` — the connecting map `Γ(U₀ ⊓ U₁) →ₗ[k] HModule (X.moduleKSheaf k) 1`
40	  ("class of a section on the overlap").
41	* `TwoCover.h1CokEquiv : HModule (X.moduleKSheaf k) 1 ≃ₗ[k] H1Cok k X U₀ U₁`.
42	* Compatibility: `h1CokEquiv_delta` (`h1CokEquiv ∘ delta = Quotient.mk`),
43	  `delta_surjective`, `delta_diff`, `delta_resHom_left/right` and
44	  `h1Cok_mk_resHom_left/right` (classes of sections extending to `U₀` or `U₁` vanish).
45	
46	The `k`-module structure on `Γ(X, U)` is `Scheme.overModule` (restriction of scalars
47	along the structure morphism), activated as a local instance as in
48	`AlgebraicJacobian.Cohomology.ModuleKSheaf`.

68	    (Opens.grothendieckTopology (X : TopCat)).MayerVietorisSquare :=

88	`k`-modules on the small Zariski site of `X`, two opens with `U₀ ⊔ U₁ = ⊤` and
89	vanishing `H¹'(U₀, F)`, `H¹'(U₁, F)`, the degree-one cohomology of the site is the

93	    (hcov : U₀ ⊔ U₁ = ⊤)

112	attribute [local instance] Scheme.overModule
113	
114	/-- The restriction-difference map `Γ(X, U₀) × Γ(X, U₁) →ₗ[k] Γ(X, U₀ ⊓ U₁)`,
115	`(s₀, s₁) ↦ s₀|_{U₀ ⊓ U₁} - s₁|_{U₀ ⊓ U₁}` (see `TwoCover.diff_apply`), with the
116	`k`-module structures of `Scheme.overModule`. -/
117	noncomputable def diff : (Γ(X, U₀) × Γ(X, U₁)) →ₗ[k] Γ(X, U₀ ⊓ U₁) :=
118	  ((X.moduleKSheaf k).obj.map (homOfLE (inf_le_left : U₀ ⊓ U₁ ≤ U₀)).op).hom.comp
119	      (LinearMap.fst k _ _) -
120	    ((X.moduleKSheaf k).obj.map (homOfLE (inf_le_right : U₀ ⊓ U₁ ≤ U₁)).op).hom.comp
121	      (LinearMap.snd k _ _)
122	
123	lemma diff_apply (t : Γ(X, U₀) × Γ(X, U₁)) :
124	    diff k X U₀ U₁ t = X.resHom inf_le_left t.1 - X.resHom inf_le_right t.2 :=
125	  rfl
126	
127	/-- The two-cover difference map is the Mayer–Vietoris restriction-difference map of the
128	associated square. -/
129	lemma diff_eq_moduleDiff (hcov : U₀ ⊔ U₁ = ⊤) :
130	    diff k X U₀ U₁ = (X.twoCoverSquare U₀ U₁ hcov).moduleDiff (X.moduleKSheaf k) :=
131	  rfl
132	
133	/-- **The two-cover H¹ cokernel carrier**: the cokernel of the restriction-difference
134	map, `Γ(X, U₀ ⊓ U₁) ⧸ range (TwoCover.diff)`. For `U₀, U₁` an affine open cover this is
135	`H¹ₖ(X, 𝒪)` (see `TwoCover.h1CokEquiv`); it is a plain quotient of section modules, so
136	`Module.finrank` arguments can be run on it directly. -/
137	noncomputable abbrev H1Cok : Type u :=
138	  Γ(X, U₀ ⊓ U₁) ⧸ LinearMap.range (diff k X U₀ U₁)
139	
140	/-- A section extending to `U₀` has vanishing class in `H1Cok`. -/
141	lemma h1Cok_mk_resHom_left (t : Γ(X, U₀)) :
142	    (Submodule.Quotient.mk (X.resHom inf_le_left t) : H1Cok k X U₀ U₁) = 0 := by
143	  rw [Submodule.Quotient.mk_eq_zero]
144	  exact ⟨(t, 0), by rw [diff_apply]; simp⟩
145	
146	/-- A section extending to `U₁` has vanishing class in `H1Cok`. -/
147	lemma h1Cok_mk_resHom_right (t : Γ(X, U₁)) :
148	    (Submodule.Quotient.mk (X.resHom inf_le_right t) : H1Cok k X U₀ U₁) = 0 := by
149	  rw [Submodule.Quotient.mk_eq_zero]
150	  refine ⟨(0, -t), ?_⟩
151	  rw [diff_apply]
152	  simp

156	variable (hcov : U₀ ⊔ U₁ = ⊤)
157	
158	/-- The two-cover connecting map: the degree-one cohomology class of a section on the
159	overlap `U₀ ⊓ U₁`, in the cohomology `Sheaf.HModule` of the small Zariski site of `X`. -/
160	noncomputable def delta :
161	    Γ(X, U₀ ⊓ U₁) →ₗ[k] Sheaf.HModule (X.moduleKSheaf k) 1 :=
162	  ((Sheaf.HModule.linearEquivHModule' (isTerminalTop : IsTerminal (⊤ : X.Opens))
163	      (X.moduleKSheaf k) 1).symm.toLinearMap).comp
164	    ((X.twoCoverSquare U₀ U₁ hcov).moduleDelta (X.moduleKSheaf k))
165	
166	/-- The connecting class of a difference of restrictions vanishes. -/
167	lemma delta_diff (t : Γ(X, U₀) × Γ(X, U₁)) :
168	    delta k X U₀ U₁ hcov (diff k X U₀ U₁ t) = 0 := by
169	  have h : (X.twoCoverSquare U₀ U₁ hcov).moduleDelta (X.moduleKSheaf k)
170	      (diff k X U₀ U₁ t) = 0 :=
171	    (X.twoCoverSquare U₀ U₁ hcov).moduleDelta_moduleDiff (X.moduleKSheaf k) t
172	  rw [show delta k X U₀ U₁ hcov (diff k X U₀ U₁ t) =
173	      (Sheaf.HModule.linearEquivHModule' (isTerminalTop : IsTerminal (⊤ : X.Opens))
174	          (X.moduleKSheaf k) 1).symm
175	        ((X.twoCoverSquare U₀ U₁ hcov).moduleDelta (X.moduleKSheaf k)
176	          (diff k X U₀ U₁ t)) from rfl, h]
177	  exact map_zero _
178	
179	/-- The connecting class of a section extending to `U₀` vanishes. -/
180	lemma delta_resHom_left (t : Γ(X, U₀)) :
181	    delta k X U₀ U₁ hcov (X.resHom inf_le_left t) = 0 := by
182	  have h : X.resHom inf_le_left t = diff k X U₀ U₁ (t, 0) := by
183	    rw [diff_apply]
184	    simp
185	  rw [h, delta_diff]
186	
187	/-- The connecting class of a section extending to `U₁` vanishes. -/
188	lemma delta_resHom_right (t : Γ(X, U₁)) :
189	    delta k X U₀ U₁ hcov (X.resHom inf_le_right t) = 0 := by
190	  have h : X.resHom inf_le_right t = -diff k X U₀ U₁ (0, t) := by
191	    rw [diff_apply]
192	    simp
193	  rw [h, map_neg, delta_diff, neg_zero]

198	/-- For an affine two-cover, the connecting map is surjective: every degree-one class
199	comes from a section on the overlap. -/
200	lemma delta_surjective : Function.Surjective (delta k X U₀ U₁ hcov) := by
201	  haveI : Subsingleton
202	      (Sheaf.HModule' (X.moduleKSheaf k) (X.twoCoverSquare U₀ U₁ hcov).X₂ 1) :=

204	  haveI : Subsingleton
205	      (Sheaf.HModule' (X.moduleKSheaf k) (X.twoCoverSquare U₀ U₁ hcov).X₃ 1) :=
206	    hU₁.subsingleton_moduleKSheaf_hModule'_one k
207	  intro y
208	  obtain ⟨s, hs⟩ := (X.twoCoverSquare U₀ U₁ hcov).moduleDelta_surjective (X.moduleKSheaf k)
209	    ((Sheaf.HModule.linearEquivHModule' (isTerminalTop : IsTerminal (⊤ : X.Opens))
210	      (X.moduleKSheaf k) 1) y)
211	  refine ⟨s, ?_⟩
212	  rw [show delta k X U₀ U₁ hcov s =
213	      (Sheaf.HModule.linearEquivHModule' (isTerminalTop : IsTerminal (⊤ : X.Opens))
214	          (X.moduleKSheaf k) 1).symm
215	        ((X.twoCoverSquare U₀ U₁ hcov).moduleDelta (X.moduleKSheaf k) s) from rfl, hs,
216	    LinearEquiv.symm_apply_apply]

218	/-- **The two-affine-cover H¹ cokernel bridge.** For a scheme `X` over `Spec k` and two

221	restriction-difference map on sections:
222	`H¹ₖ(X, 𝒪) ≃ₗ[k] Γ(U₀ ⊓ U₁) ⧸ range((s₀, s₁) ↦ s₀|∩ - s₁|∩)`.
223	The inverse sends the class of a section on the overlap to its connecting class
224	(`TwoCover.h1CokEquiv_delta`). -/
225	noncomputable def h1CokEquiv :
226	    Sheaf.HModule (X.moduleKSheaf k) 1 ≃ₗ[k] H1Cok k X U₀ U₁ :=
227	  letI : Subsingleton
228	      (Sheaf.HModule' (X.moduleKSheaf k) (X.twoCoverSquare U₀ U₁ hcov).X₂ 1) :=
229	    hU₀.subsingleton_moduleKSheaf_hModule'_one k
230	  letI : Subsingleton
231	      (Sheaf.HModule' (X.moduleKSheaf k) (X.twoCoverSquare U₀ U₁ hcov).X₃ 1) :=
232	    hU₁.subsingleton_moduleKSheaf_hModule'_one k
233	  (Sheaf.HModule.linearEquivHModule' (isTerminalTop : IsTerminal (⊤ : X.Opens))
234	      (X.moduleKSheaf k) 1).trans
235	    ((X.twoCoverSquare U₀ U₁ hcov).h1LinearEquiv (X.moduleKSheaf k)).symm
236	
237	/-- Compatibility of the bridge with the connecting map: the bridge sends the connecting
238	class of a section on the overlap to its class in the cokernel. -/
239	lemma h1CokEquiv_delta (s : Γ(X, U₀ ⊓ U₁)) :
240	    h1CokEquiv k X U₀ U₁ hcov hU₀ hU₁ (delta k X U₀ U₁ hcov s) =
241	      Submodule.Quotient.mk s := by
242	  haveI : Subsingleton
243	      (Sheaf.HModule' (X.moduleKSheaf k) (X.twoCoverSquare U₀ U₁ hcov).X₂ 1) :=
244	    hU₀.subsingleton_moduleKSheaf_hModule'_one k
245	  haveI : Subsingleton
246	      (Sheaf.HModule' (X.moduleKSheaf k) (X.twoCoverSquare U₀ U₁ hcov).X₃ 1) :=
247	    hU₁.subsingleton_moduleKSheaf_hModule'_one k
248	  apply ((X.twoCoverSquare U₀ U₁ hcov).h1LinearEquiv (X.moduleKSheaf k)).injective
249	  calc ((X.twoCoverSquare U₀ U₁ hcov).h1LinearEquiv (X.moduleKSheaf k))
250	        (h1CokEquiv k X U₀ U₁ hcov hU₀ hU₁ (delta k X U₀ U₁ hcov s))
251	      = ((X.twoCoverSquare U₀ U₁ hcov).h1LinearEquiv (X.moduleKSheaf k))
252	          (((X.twoCoverSquare U₀ U₁ hcov).h1LinearEquiv (X.moduleKSheaf k)).symm

261	    _ = ((X.twoCoverSquare U₀ U₁ hcov).h1LinearEquiv (X.moduleKSheaf k))
262	          (Submodule.Quotient.mk s) :=
263	        (MayerVietorisSquare.h1LinearEquiv_mk (S := X.twoCoverSquare U₀ U₁ hcov)
264	          (X.moduleKSheaf k) s).symm

1	/-
2	Copyright (c) 2026 The AlgebraicJacobian authors. All rights reserved.
3	Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
4	Authors: The AlgebraicJacobian Contributors
5	-/
6	import AlgebraicJacobian.Curve.Basic
7	import AlgebraicJacobian.Curve.GeometricallyReduced
8	import AlgebraicJacobian.Curve.P1Charts
9	import AlgebraicJacobian.Curve.RationalToP1
10	
11	/-!
12	# A finite morphism from the curve to the projective line
13	
14	For the smooth, proper, geometrically irreducible curve `C` over `k`, this file is about the
15	existence and the basic consequences of a **finite** `k`-morphism `π : C ⟶ ℙ¹`.
16	
17	## Contents
18	
19	* `AlgebraicGeometry.IsFinite.of_locallyQuasiFinite_of_comp` — the general Zariski-main-theorem
20	  reduction: a locally quasi-finite morphism which is proper over a separated base is finite.
21	* `AlgebraicGeometry.isFinite_toP1_of_locallyQuasiFinite` — the specialization: a locally
22	  quasi-finite `k`-morphism from the proper curve `C` to `ℙ¹` is finite.
23	* `AlgebraicGeometry.exists_isFinite_toP1_of_locallyQuasiFinite` — the same, in existential
24	  form: to produce a finite `π : C ⟶ ℙ¹` over `k` it suffices to produce a locally
25	  quasi-finite one.
26	* Preimage bookkeeping for a finite `π`, consumed by the two-lattice finiteness argument for
27	  `H¹(C, 𝒪_C)`: the preimages of the two standard charts are affine opens covering `C`
28	  (`isAffineOpen_preimage_chartOpen`, `preimage_chartOpen_sup`), and the section ring of each
29	  preimage is module-finite over the section ring of the chart (`finite_app_chartOpen`).
30	* `AlgebraicGeometry.exists_isFinite_toP1` — the **existence** of a finite `π : C ⟶ ℙ¹` over
31	  `k`, by spreading out a transcendental rational function
32	  (`AlgebraicJacobian.Curve.RationalToP1`) and applying the reduction above; see its
33	  docstring for the proof route.
34	-/
35	
36	set_option autoImplicit false
37	
38	universe u
39	
40	open CategoryTheory MvPolynomial
41	
42	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
43	
44	/-- **Zariski's main theorem, cancellation form**: a locally quasi-finite morphism `π` such
45	that `π ≫ g` is proper and `g` is separated is finite. (Properness of `π` follows by
46	cancellation, and a proper locally quasi-finite morphism is finite.) -/
47	theorem IsFinite.of_locallyQuasiFinite_of_comp {X Y S : Scheme.{u}}
48	    (π : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y ⟶ S) [LocallyQuasiFinite π] [IsSeparated g] [IsProper (π ≫ g)] :
49	    IsFinite π :=
50	  have : IsProper π := IsProper.of_comp π g
51	  IsFinite.of_isProper_of_locallyQuasiFinite π
52	
53	variable {k : Type u} [Field k]
54	
55	section ZMT
56	
57	variable {X : Scheme.{u}}
58	
59	/-- A locally quasi-finite `k`-morphism from a scheme which is proper over `k` to the
60	projective line is finite. This is the Zariski-main-theorem half of the construction of the
61	finite map `C ⟶ ℙ¹`: it reduces finiteness to local quasi-finiteness. -/
62	theorem isFinite_toP1_of_locallyQuasiFinite (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) [IsProper f]
63	    (π : X ⟶ P1 k) [LocallyQuasiFinite π] (hπ : π ≫ P1.structureMap k = f) :
64	    IsFinite π :=
65	  have : IsProper (π ≫ P1.structureMap k) := hπ ▸ inferInstance
66	  IsFinite.of_locallyQuasiFinite_of_comp π (P1.structureMap k)
67	
68	end ZMT
69	
70	/-- To produce a finite `k`-morphism `C ⟶ ℙ¹` it suffices to produce a locally quasi-finite
71	one; Zariski's main theorem upgrades it. -/
72	theorem exists_isFinite_toP1_of_locallyQuasiFinite {C : Over (Spec (.of k))} [IsProper C.hom]
73	    (h : ∃ π : C.left ⟶ P1 k, LocallyQuasiFinite π ∧ π ≫ P1.structureMap k = C.hom) :
74	    ∃ π : C.left ⟶ P1 k, IsFinite π ∧ π ≫ P1.structureMap k = C.hom := by
75	  obtain ⟨π, hqf, hcomp⟩ := h
76	  exact ⟨π, isFinite_toP1_of_locallyQuasiFinite C.hom π hcomp, hcomp⟩
77	
78	variable {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
79	  [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
80	
81	/-- **Existence of a finite map to the projective line**: on the smooth, proper,
82	geometrically irreducible curve `C/k` there is a finite `k`-morphism `π : C ⟶ ℙ¹`.
83	
84	This is the keystone the two-lattice finiteness argument for `H¹(C, 𝒪_C)` consumes.
85	
86	Proof route (see `informal/route-decision.md`, Wave 1 item 4):
87	1. `C` is integral (smooth ⟹ geometrically reduced, `AlgebraicJacobian.Curve.
88	   GeometricallyReduced`, plus geometric irreducibility, `AlgebraicJacobian.Curve.Basic`),
89	   and the function field of `C` contains an element transcendental over `k`: the étale
90	   coordinate of a standard smooth chart of relative dimension `1`
91	   (`SmoothOfRelativeDimension.exists_transcendental_functionField`, via the structure
92	   theorem for standard smooth algebras of Stacks 00T7);
93	2. the transcendental function spreads out to a morphism `π : C ⟶ ℙ¹` over `k`: the stalks
94	   of `C` are valuation rings (localizations of the Dedekind chart rings,
95	   `AlgebraicJacobian.Curve.DedekindSections` and `Curve.StalksDVR`), so at each point
96	   either `f` or `1/f` is a regular germ; the two chart morphisms agree generically by the
97	   gluing identity `P1.fromSpecChart_units`, so the associated rational map `C ⤏ ℙ¹` is
98	   defined everywhere (`AlgebraicJacobian.Curve.RationalToP1`);
99	3. `π` maps the generic point to the generic point (transcendence again), hence has finite
100	   fibers on the height-one Noetherian space `C`, hence is locally quasi-finite;
101	4. conclude with `exists_isFinite_toP1_of_locallyQuasiFinite` (Zariski's main theorem). -/
102	theorem exists_isFinite_toP1 :
103	    ∃ π : C.left ⟶ P1 k, IsFinite π ∧ π ≫ P1.structureMap k = C.hom :=
104	  exists_isFinite_toP1_of_locallyQuasiFinite (exists_locallyQuasiFinite_toP1 C.hom)
105	
106	/-! ### Preimage bookkeeping for a finite morphism to the projective line
107	
108	The next wave feeds these to the two-lattice/Mayer–Vietoris finiteness argument: the
109	preimages of the two standard charts form an affine cover of `C`, with section rings
110	module-finite over `k[t]`. Everything here only needs `π` finite (indeed mostly just
111	affine), not how it was constructed. -/
112	
113	section Preimages
114	
115	variable {Y : Scheme.{u}} (π : Y ⟶ P1 k)
116	
117	/-- The preimage of each standard chart of `ℙ¹` under an affine (e.g. finite) morphism is an
118	affine open. -/
119	theorem isAffineOpen_preimage_chartOpen [IsAffineHom π] (i : Fin 2) :
120	    IsAffineOpen (π ⁻¹ᵁ P1.chartOpen k i) :=
121	  (P1.isAffineOpen_chartOpen k i).preimage π
122	
123	/-- The preimages of the two standard charts of `ℙ¹` cover the source. -/
124	theorem preimage_chartOpen_sup :
125	    π ⁻¹ᵁ P1.chartOpen k 0 ⊔ π ⁻¹ᵁ P1.chartOpen k 1 = ⊤ := by
126	  refine le_antisymm le_top fun x _ => ?_
127	  have h : π.base x ∈ P1.chartOpen k 0 ⊔ P1.chartOpen k 1 := by
128	    rw [P1.chartOpen_sup]
129	    trivial
130	  rw [TopologicalSpace.Opens.mem_sup] at h ⊢
131	  exact h
132	
133	/-- For a finite morphism `π : X ⟶ ℙ¹`, the section ring of the preimage of a standard chart
134	is module-finite over the section ring of the chart (that is, over `k[t]`, via
135	`P1.chartSectionsEquiv₀`/`₁`). -/
136	theorem finite_app_chartOpen [IsFinite π] (i : Fin 2) :
137	    RingHom.Finite (π.app (P1.chartOpen k i)).hom :=
138	  π.finite_app _ (P1.isAffineOpen_chartOpen k i)
139	
140	/-- For a finite morphism `π : X ⟶ ℙ¹`, the section ring of the preimage of the chart
141	overlap is module-finite over the section ring of the overlap (that is, over the Laurent
142	polynomial ring, via `P1.overlapSectionsEquiv`). -/
143	theorem finite_app_overlap [IsFinite π] :
144	    RingHom.Finite (π.app (Proj.basicOpen (homogeneousSubmodule (Fin 2) k)
145	      (X 0 * X 1))).hom :=
146	  π.finite_app _ (P1.isAffineOpen_overlap k)
147	
148	end Preimages
149	
150	end AlgebraicGeometry

/-

-/
module

public import Mathlib.CategoryTheory.Adjunction.Limits
public import Mathlib.CategoryTheory.Comma.Over.Pullback
public import Mathlib.CategoryTheory.Limits.Constructions.Over.Products
public import Mathlib.CategoryTheory.Monoidal.CommMon_
public import Mathlib.CategoryTheory.Monoidal.Grp
public import Mathlib.CategoryTheory.Limits.Shapes.Pullback.IsPullback.Basic

/-!

# `CartesianMonoidalCategory` for `Over X`

We provide a `CartesianMonoidalCategory (Over X)` instance via pullbacks, and provide simp lemmas
for the induced `MonoidalCategory (Over X)` instance.

-/

public noncomputable section

namespace CategoryTheory.Over

open Functor Limits CartesianMonoidalCategory

variable {C : Type*} [Category* C] [HasPullbacks C]

set_option backward.defeqAttrib.useBackward true in
/-- A choice of finite products of `Over X` given by `Limits.pullback`. -/
abbrev cartesianMonoidalCategory (X : C) : CartesianMonoidalCategory (Over X) :=
  .ofChosenFiniteProducts
    ⟨asEmptyCone (Over.mk (𝟙 X)), IsTerminal.ofUniqueHom (fun Y ↦ Over.homMk Y.hom)
      fun Y m ↦ Over.OverMorphism.ext (by simpa using m.w)⟩
    fun Y Z ↦ ⟨pullbackConeEquivBinaryFan.functor.obj (pullback.cone Y.hom Z.hom),
    (pullback.isLimit _ _).pullbackConeEquivBinaryFanFunctor⟩

attribute [local instance] cartesianMonoidalCategory

/-- `Over X` is braided w.r.t. the Cartesian monoidal structure given by `Limits.pullback`. -/
abbrev braidedCategory (X : C) : BraidedCategory (Over X) :=
  .ofCartesianMonoidalCategory

attribute [local instance] braidedCategory

open MonoidalCategory

variable {X : C}

@[ext]
lemma tensorObj_ext {R : C} {S T : Over X} (f₁ f₂ : R ⟶ (S ⊗ T).left)
    (e₁ : f₁ ≫ pullback.fst _ _ = f₂ ≫ pullback.fst _ _)
    (e₂ : f₁ ≫ pullback.snd _ _ = f₂ ≫ pullback.snd _ _) : f₁ = f₂ :=
  pullback.hom_ext e₁ e₂

@[simp]
lemma tensorObj_left (R S : Over X) : (R ⊗ S).left = Limits.pullback R.hom S.hom := rfl

@[simp]
lemma tensorObj_hom (R S : Over X) : (R ⊗ S).hom = pullback.fst R.hom S.hom ≫ R.hom := rfl

@[simp]
lemma tensorUnit_left : (𝟙_ (Over X)).left = X := rfl

@[simp]
lemma tensorUnit_hom : (𝟙_ (Over X)).hom = 𝟙 X := rfl

@[simp]
lemma lift_left {R S T : Over X} (f : R ⟶ S) (g : R ⟶ T) :
    (lift f g).left = pullback.lift f.left g.left (f.w.trans g.w.symm) := rfl

@[simp]
lemma fst_left {R S : Over X} : (fst R S).left = pullback.fst _ _ := rfl

@[simp]
lemma snd_left {R S : Over X} : (snd R S).left = pullback.snd _ _ := rfl

@[simp]
lemma toUnit_left {R : Over X} : (toUnit R).left = R.hom := rfl

@[reassoc (attr := simp)]
lemma associator_hom_left_fst (R S T : Over X) :
    (α_ R S T).hom.left ≫ pullback.fst _ (pullback.fst _ _ ≫ _) =
      pullback.fst _ _ ≫ pullback.fst _ _ :=
  limit.lift_π _ _

@[reassoc (attr := simp)]
lemma associator_hom_left_snd_fst (R S T : Over X) :
    (α_ R S T).hom.left ≫ pullback.snd _ (pullback.fst _ _ ≫ _) ≫ pullback.fst _ _ =
      pullback.fst _ _ ≫ pullback.snd _ _ :=
  (limit.lift_π_assoc _ _ _).trans (limit.lift_π _ _)

@[reassoc (attr := simp)]
lemma associator_hom_left_snd_snd (R S T : Over X) :
    (α_ R S T).hom.left ≫ pullback.snd _ (pullback.fst _ _ ≫ _) ≫ pullback.snd _ _ =
      pullback.snd _ _ :=
  (limit.lift_π_assoc _ _ _).trans (limit.lift_π _ _)

@[reassoc (attr := simp)]
lemma associator_inv_left_fst_fst (R S T : Over X) :
    (α_ R S T).inv.left ≫ pullback.fst (pullback.fst _ _ ≫ _) _ ≫ pullback.fst _ _ =
      pullback.fst _ _ :=
  (limit.lift_π_assoc _ _ _).trans (limit.lift_π _ _)

@[reassoc (attr := simp)]
lemma associator_inv_left_fst_snd (R S T : Over X) :
    (α_ R S T).inv.left ≫ pullback.fst (pullback.fst _ _ ≫ _) _ ≫ pullback.snd _ _ =
      pullback.snd _ _ ≫ pullback.fst _ _ :=
  (limit.lift_π_assoc _ _ _).trans (limit.lift_π _ _)

@[reassoc (attr := simp)]
lemma associator_inv_left_snd (R S T : Over X) :
    (α_ R S T).inv.left ≫ pullback.snd (pullback.fst _ _ ≫ _) _ =
      pullback.snd _ _ ≫ pullback.snd _ _ :=
  limit.lift_π _ _

@[simp]
lemma leftUnitor_hom_left (Y : Over X) :
    (λ_ Y).hom.left = pullback.snd _ _ := rfl

@[reassoc (attr := simp)]
lemma leftUnitor_inv_left_fst (Y : Over X) :
    (λ_ Y).inv.left ≫ pullback.fst (𝟙 X) _ = Y.hom :=
  limit.lift_π _ _

@[reassoc (attr := simp)]
lemma leftUnitor_inv_left_snd (Y : Over X) :
    (λ_ Y).inv.left ≫ pullback.snd (𝟙 X) _ = 𝟙 Y.left :=
  limit.lift_π _ _

@[simp]
lemma rightUnitor_hom_left (Y : Over X) :
    (ρ_ Y).hom.left = pullback.fst _ (𝟙 X) := rfl

@[reassoc (attr := simp)]
lemma rightUnitor_inv_left_fst (Y : Over X) :
    (ρ_ Y).inv.left ≫ pullback.fst _ (𝟙 X) = 𝟙 _ :=
  limit.lift_π _ _

@[reassoc (attr := simp)]
lemma rightUnitor_inv_left_snd (Y : Over X) :
    (ρ_ Y).inv.left ≫ pullback.snd _ (𝟙 X) = Y.hom :=
  limit.lift_π _ _

lemma whiskerLeft_left {R S T : Over X} (f : S ⟶ T) :
    (R ◁ f).left = pullback.map _ _ _ _ (𝟙 _) f.left (𝟙 _) (by simp) (by simp) := rfl

@[reassoc (attr := simp)]
lemma whiskerLeft_left_fst {R S T : Over X} (f : S ⟶ T) :
    (R ◁ f).left ≫ pullback.fst _ _ = pullback.fst _ _ :=
  (limit.lift_π _ _).trans (Category.comp_id _)

@[reassoc (attr := simp)]
lemma whiskerLeft_left_snd {R S T : Over X} (f : S ⟶ T) :
    (R ◁ f).left ≫ pullback.snd _ _ = pullback.snd _ _ ≫ f.left :=
  limit.lift_π _ _

lemma whiskerRight_left {R S T : Over X} (f : S ⟶ T) :
    (f ▷ R).left = pullback.map _ _ _ _ f.left (𝟙 _) (𝟙 _) (by simp) (by simp) := rfl

@[reassoc (attr := simp)]
lemma whiskerRight_left_fst {R S T : Over X} (f : S ⟶ T) :

lemma whiskerRight_left_snd {R S T : Over X} (f : S ⟶ T) :

lemma tensorHom_left {R S T U : Over X} (f : R ⟶ S) (g : T ⟶ U) :
    (f ⊗ₘ g).left = pullback.map _ _ _ _ f.left g.left (𝟙 _) (by simp) (by simp) := rfl

@[reassoc (attr := simp)]
lemma tensorHom_left_fst {S U : C} {R T : Over X} (fS : S ⟶ X) (fU : U ⟶ X)

@[simps! -isSimp mul one]
abbrev monObjMkPullbackSnd [MonObj (Over.mk f)] : MonObj (Over.mk <| pullback.snd f g) :=
  ((Over.pullback g).mapMon.obj <| .mk <| .mk f).mon

attribute [local instance] monObjMkPullbackSnd

instance isCommMonObj_mk_pullbackSnd [MonObj (Over.mk f)] [IsCommMonObj (Over.mk f)] :
    IsCommMonObj (Over.mk <| pullback.snd f g) :=
  ((Over.pullback g).mapCommMon.obj <| .mk <| .mk f).comm

/-- The pullback of a monoid object is a monoid object. -/
@[simps! -isSimp mul one]
abbrev grpObjMkPullbackSnd [GrpObj (Over.mk f)] : GrpObj (Over.mk (pullback.snd f g)) :=
  ((Over.pullback g).mapGrp.obj <| .mk <| .mk f).grp

attribute [local simp] monObjMkPullbackSnd_one in
instance isMonHom_pullbackFst_id_right [MonObj (Over.mk f)] :
    IsMonHom <| Over.homMk (U := Over.mk <| pullback.snd f (𝟙 X)) (V := Over.mk f)
      (pullback.fst f (𝟙 X)) (pullback.condition.trans <| by simp) where
  mul_hom := by
    ext
    dsimp [monObjMkPullbackSnd_mul]
    simp only [Category.assoc, limit.lift_π, PullbackCone.mk_pt, PullbackCone.mk_π_app]
    simp only [← Category.assoc]

9	/-!
10	# The Jacobian challenge — statement file (with field base change)
11	
12	This is the single, self-contained **statement file** of the project: it collects every
13	definition, instance, and theorem needed to *state* the main result, and nothing else. A reviewer
14	reads this one file, compares it against the original challenge (`references/challenge.lean`, by
15	Christian Merten) and its base-change extension, and is convinced the project formalizes the right
16	thing. The genuinely-missing pieces are `sorry`; the base-change scaffolding (`baseChange`, the
17	stability instances, `idIso`, `compIso`, and `Jacobian.congr` derived from `Jacobian.functor`) is
18	genuinely proved here. Proofs of the `sorry`s live in the rest of the `AlgebraicJacobian/` tree and
19	must not weaken or restate any signature below.
20	
21	By a **smooth curve** we mean a geometrically irreducible, smooth scheme of relative dimension one
22	over a field, proper over that field.
23	
24	## Main definitions
25	
26	* `AlgebraicGeometry.genus` — genus of a proper, smooth curve.
27	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Jacobian` — the Jacobian of a proper, smooth curve.
28	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Jacobian.ofCurve` — the Abel–Jacobi map associated to a `k`-rational point.
29	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Jacobian.functor` — functoriality of the Jacobian, bundled as a single
30	  contravariant functor `(Curve k)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Grp (Over (Spec k))`.
31	
32	## Main theorems
33	
34	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Jacobian.smoothOfRelativeDimension_genus` — the Jacobian is smooth of relative
35	  dimension `g = genus C`.
36	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Jacobian.exists_unique_ofCurve_comp` — the universal property: the Jacobian is
37	  the Albanese variety of `C`.
38	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Jacobian.baseChangeIso` — the Jacobian commutes with base change of fields,
39	  together with the identity/cocycle coherences (`baseChangeIso_id`, `baseChangeIso_comp`) and the
40	  Abel–Jacobi compatibility `baseChange_ofCurve`.
41	
42	## Notes
43	
44	`noncomputable` is on the data-carrying declarations: their honest realizations rest on
45	noncomputable Mathlib constructions. Names, argument types, and argument order are verbatim from
46	the challenge; the `noncomputable` modifier is not a signature change.
47	-/

65	/-- The category of smooth, proper, geometrically irreducible curves over `k`, with morphisms the
66	morphisms of `k`-schemes. -/
67	structure Curve (k : Type u) [Field k] where
68	  /-- The underlying `k`-scheme. -/
69	  carrier : Over (Spec (.of k))
70	  [isProper : IsProper carrier.hom]
71	  [smoothOfRelativeDimension : SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 carrier.hom]
72	  [geometricallyIrreducible : GeometricallyIrreducible carrier.hom]

77	  Hom X Y := X.carrier ⟶ Y.carrier
78	  id X := 𝟙 X.carrier
79	  comp f g := f ≫ g
80	  id_comp := Category.id_comp
81	  comp_id := Category.comp_id

85	/-- The genus of a smooth proper curve: the `k`-dimension of the first cohomology group
86	`H¹(C, 𝒪_C)` of the structure sheaf, viewed as a sheaf of `k`-modules on the small Zariski
87	site of `C` (`Scheme.moduleKSheaf`), with cohomology the `Ext` from the constant sheaf
88	(`CategoryTheory.Sheaf.HModule`). Finite-dimensionality of `H¹` is proved downstream. -/
89	noncomputable def genus (C : Over (Spec (.of k))) [IsProper C.hom]
90	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom] : ℕ :=
91	  letI : C.left.Over (Spec (.of k)) := .ofHom C.hom
92	  Module.finrank k (Sheaf.HModule (C.left.moduleKSheaf k) 1)

98	    Over (Spec (.of k)) :=

138	`f : C ⟶ A` with `f(P) = 0` factors uniquely through the Jacobian of `C`. In other words,
139	`Jacobian C` is the Albanese variety of `C`.

162	/-! ## Base change of fields
163	
164	Base change of `k`-schemes along `k → L` sends `X` to `X ×_{Spec k} Spec L`. These definitions and

168	/-- Base change of `k`-schemes along a field homomorphism `k → L`, i.e. `X ↦ X ×_{Spec k} Spec L`.
169	-/
170	noncomputable abbrev baseChange (k L : Type u) [Field k] [Field L] [Algebra k L] :
171	    Over (Spec (.of k)) ⥤ Over (Spec (.of L)) :=
172	  Over.pullback (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k L)))
173

175	    [IsProper C.hom] : IsProper ((baseChange k L).obj C).hom :=

184	    SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 ((baseChange k L).obj C).hom :=
185	  have : MorphismProperty.IsStableUnderBaseChange (@SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1) :=

187	  MorphismProperty.baseChange_obj (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k L))) C inferInstance

211	noncomputable def baseChange.idIso (k : Type u) [Field k] :
212	    baseChange k k ≅ 𝟭 (Over (Spec (.of k))) :=
213	  eqToIso (by
214	    change Over.pullback (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k k))) = Over.pullback (𝟙 _)
215	    rw [Algebra.algebraMap_self, CommRingCat.ofHom_id, Spec.map_id]) ≪≫ Over.pullbackId
216	
217	/-- Base change along a tower `k → L → M` is the composite of the two base changes. -/
218	noncomputable def baseChange.compIso (k L M : Type u) [Field k] [Field L] [Field M]
219	    [Algebra k L] [Algebra L M] [Algebra k M] [IsScalarTower k L M] :
220	    baseChange k M ≅ baseChange k L ⋙ baseChange L M :=
221	  eqToIso (by
222	    change Over.pullback (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k M))) =
223	      Over.pullback (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap L M)) ≫
224	        Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k L)))
225	    rw [← Spec.map_comp, ← CommRingCat.ofHom_comp, ← IsScalarTower.algebraMap_eq]) ≪≫
226	    Over.pullbackComp _ _
